about: Standing OKs from the user, as structured records. This is the sample's starting set: replace your-org/your-repo and your-login with your own repo and GitHub login, and keep shepherd_mode observe until you trust the proposals. Only the conductor edits this file, and only on the user's explicit words; it mirrors every change to CAO memory and bumps policy_version. check_mandate.py reads it before every outside action.
push_urls_about: The only URL a push action may publish to, per repo. The publisher pushes and runs ls-remote against this exact URL (never the name origin). Its pre-write check refuses unless the worktree's fetch and push URLs for origin are each exactly this one URL (only a trailing .git is normalised) and no url.*.insteadOf or pushInsteadOf rewrite exists.

conditions.what: Fast-forward fix commits for CI fixes and review feedback on the user's own open PRs.
never: amend, rebase or rewrite pushed history
before_push: ls-remote head equals the expected remote head
our own checks pass: focused set + repo-root guards + test/decisions
independent pre-push review for a large or risky change
no competing PR already has the change (gh pr list --search)
git rev-parse <branch> equals the approved new head; push exactly git push <push_urls URL> <new head>:refs/heads/<branch>, never a bare branch name or the name origin
conditions.after_push: ls-remote read-back equals the new head; report it to the conductor

conditions.what: gh pr update-branch <n> (merge update, never --rebase) for an approved, green PR that is BEHIND, also when auto-merge is already armed. The auto-merge rule's order: arm first, update later. One worker does only this, reports the new head and stops. Where branch protection keeps approvals on a merge from main, update-branch keeps the approval; a fix push dismisses it.
requires: automerge_gate.py --action update_branch prints UPDATE_BRANCH <head> (it includes the hold-on-findings window check)
check_mandate.py --expect-head <head> --remote-head <ls-remote> right before the command
conditions.never_prs_about: PR numbers that must never auto-merge or be updated (for example a release PR). Integers only.

conditions.what: Mark ONE review or comment as not holding (bin/holds.py clear), bound to its id and the sha256 of its exact body, after reading it: for clean bodies the keyword scan misreads, such as 'APPROVE (0 P1, 0 P2, 0 P3) ... Findings: None.'

the conductor read the same body file and replied GO <wid>
the conductor recorded the GO in state/go.jsonl itself (writer_role conductor) with this item and body sha256
never: clear a body with a severity-tagged finding (holds.py refuses; those wait for a newer non-merge commit or the user's decline)
